statements.impact_statement: The kernel of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, kernel-rt and MRG 2 (Red Hat's securelevel patches) mishandled the secure_boot flag across a kexec reboot. Not that code: under Secure Boot the shipped kernel is locked down (lockdown LSM, not securelevel), which refuses kexec_load and requires a signed image for kexec_file_load, and kexec_file_load hands the secure_boot flag to the next kernel. Shipped config: CONFIG_SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM=y, CONFIG_LOCK_DOWN_IN_SECURE_BOOT=y, CONFIG_KEXEC_SIG=y, CONFIG_KEXEC_BZIMAGE_VERIFY_SIG=y; Ubuntu source: arch/x86/kernel/kexec-bzimage64.c:209, kernel/kexec.c:222, kernel/kexec_file.c:195. Checked by scripts/kernel_vex.py.

statements.impact_statement: Fedora Linux kernels from 6.12 on left lockdown disabled when booted with Secure Boot (CVE: 'affects only Fedora Linux'; Ubuntu's tracker, upstream: 'Red Hat specific lockdown regression'). Not that code: the shipped kernel locks itself down (integrity) when it is booted with EFI Secure Boot. Shipped config: CONFIG_SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM=y, CONFIG_SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM_EARLY=y, CONFIG_LOCK_DOWN_IN_SECURE_BOOT=y; Ubuntu source: arch/x86/kernel/setup.c:1018. Checked by scripts/kernel_vex.py.
